nodes.text: INSTANT · ON-DEVICE AI The provided document is a summary of the Constitution (specifically Articles 1, 2, and 3) which outlines the federal structure of the United States government. Main points: • Legislative Power: Vests all legislative powers in Congress, consisting of the Senate and House of Representatives; any smaller number may adjourn or compel attendance under respective rules. A majority of both Houses constitutes a quorum to conduct business. • Executive Power: The President approves bills from both Houses that become laws if returned within ten days; otherwise they remain valid unless adjusted by two-thirds agreement in the Senate or House. No state enters treaties without congressional consent, and debts contracted before the Constitution are valid against it. • Election Process: The President is elected electors from states, requiring a majority of States to choose. If no Person holds a majority among Electors, the House chooses the President by Ballot from five highest ranked candidates on the List. Summary of all 9 pages.
